claim: Château de Noirmoutier museum is open 4 April–15 November 2026, with adult tickets at €8 and a free-access courtyard.
quote: Du 4 April 2026 au 15 November 2026 ... General admission: €8.00 ... Reduced rate: €5.00 ... Family pass: €21.00

claim: In 2026 the château hosts the special exhibition 'Hissez haut! Quand l'homme prend la mer' on the island's sailors, with daily 10am–7pm hours in July/August.
quote: Hissez haut! Quand l'homme prend la mer ... In July and August, it's open daily from 10am to 7pm. The castle courtyard remains open daily from 10am to 6pm

claim: The Bois de la Chaize is a 110-hectare protected forest (listed 1936) of holm oaks, maritime pines, strawberry trees and mimosas stretching 2 km along the coast, with over 100 belle-époque villas; Renoir called it 'as beautiful as the South of France'.
quote: Over 100 villas were constructed during the late 19th and early 20th centuries ... The 110-hectare forest spans over 2 kilometers along the coast ... The site earned protected status in 1936 and even attracted painter Auguste Renoir

claim: Plage des Dames became Noirmoutier's first seaside-tourism beach after Jules Piet's Société des bains de mer moved its bathing cabins there in 1863 for shelter from the wind.
quote: En 1859, Jules Piet created the 'Société des bains de mer de Noirmoutier' and installed cabins on Plage des Souzeaux; four years later, the company moved to Plage des Dames because it was more sheltered from winds

claim: The Phare de la Pointe des Dames is an 18.7 m square white-painted keeper-house lighthouse built in 1867, automated since 2002, listed as a historic monument in 2011 and not open to visitors.
quote: En 1867, construction d'une tourelle carrée de 18,70 m ... très typique comme maison-phare ... ne se visite pas ... registered as historical monuments on November 29, 2011

claim: The Phare du Pilier on the offshore Île du Pilier was first built in 1829 (rebuilt 1877) — not 1727 — and was automated in 1996.
quote: En 1829, construction d'une tour cylindrique en maçonnerie de pierre de taille de 29,50 m ... The current lighthouse was automated in 1996

claim: O'Abandonado runs day-trip boat excursions to Île du Pilier from L'Herbaudière port on Sundays in July–August (10:30am–6pm), €70 adult / €45 child under 13, with landings restricted in summer to protect nesting gulls.
quote: Departures from L'Herbaudière Port are at 10:30 AM with returns around 6:00 PM ... Trips are only offered in July and August to respect the seagull nesting period ... €70 for adults and €45 for children under 13

claim: The Réserve Naturelle Nationale des Marais de Müllembourg, established 30 August 1994 on Noirmoutier's east coast, covers 48.39 ha managed by LPO, hosts 500 plant taxa and over 250 bird species, and shelters 5,000–10,000 waders at high tide.
quote: Created on August 30, 1994 ... 48.39 hectares ... 500 plant taxa ... 5 to 10,000 wading birds representing 20% of the bay population. Over 250 bird species have been documented ... LPO France oversees

claim: Müllembourg's nesting species include shelduck, pied avocet, ringed plover and common tern, with bar-tailed godwit, dunlin, grey plover and black-winged stilt among the migrating waders.
quote: Several remarkable bird species breed at the site including Shelduck, Pied Avocet, Ringed Plover, and Common Tern ... Wader species include Bar-tailed Godwit, Dunlin, Common Ringed Plover, Grey Plover, Avocet and Black-winged Stilt

claim: Some 100 sauniers personally guide free tours of their salt marshes from June to September, with 15 visitable salterns listed (mostly in L'Épine and La Guérinière) and salt available to buy direct.
quote: About 100 salt makers operate on the island and personally conduct visits to their own marshes ... offered from June to September ... 15 available salterns, mostly concentrated in L'Epine and La Guérinière

claim: Salt marshes cover roughly a third of Noirmoutier's surface and produce fleur de sel that crystallises at the surface of the pools after about 48 hours of evaporation in hot easterly winds.
quote: Salterns are typical of the scenery on Noirmoutier Island, covering a third of the island ... the concentration of salt slowly rises over 48 hours ... delicate crystals of fleur de sel ... shimmer at the surface of the pools

claim: La Guérinière's south-coast beaches are fine-sand and gently sloping with water about 3 °C warmer than the east coast, making them the family-swim choice; landmarks include the mills of Plage de la Court and the blockhouses of Plage de la Cantine.
quote: made only of fine sand, sloping gently into the sea ... The temperature of the water is almost always higher (by about 3°C) than on the east coast ... mills on the Plage de la Court and the blockhouses of the Plage de la Cantine

claim: The Passage du Gois is a 4.2 km tidal causeway to the mainland passable only from ~90 min before to 90 min after low tide, with rescue towers along the route for stranded crossers.
quote: The Gois Passage is a 4.2 km long, sometimes flooded road ... You can travel to or leave Noirmoutier Island via the Gois from 90 minutes before to 90 minutes after low tide ... Rescue towers located all along the Passage du Gois

claim: The causeway is precisely 4.125 km long, floods twice daily, and was the site of a famous 1999 Tour de France crash that split the peloton on its slippery surface.
quote: 4.125 kilometres (2.6 mi) long... floods twice a day during high tide... slippery conditions caused a significant crash that created a six-minute split in the peloton.

claim: Low tides at L'Herbaudière for early June 2026 fall around midday — June 6 (Sat) at 03:11 and 15:29, June 7 (Sun) at 03:57 and 16:22 — with SHOM (maree.shom.fr) as the authoritative source.
quote: June 6: 03:11 and 15:29; June 7: 03:57 and 16:22... Forecasts for L'Herbaudière come from the hydrographic and oceanographic marine service of France (SHOM).

claim: At high tide water covers the road by 1.5 to 3 m or more depending on coefficient; the bay is renowned for pêche à pied — locals gather clams, cockles and oysters on the exposed sandbanks at low tide.
quote: at high tide, it is completely submerged, with the water reaching between 1.5 and 3 m, or even more depending on tidal coefficients... large sandy expanses open up, rich in all kinds of shellfish. Locals take buckets, shovels, baskets and collect shells, shrimps and oysters.

claim: Tourist offices in Beauvoir-sur-Mer and Noirmoutier post precise tide schedules at the panneau-horaire on each side, and if caught by the tide you must abandon the vehicle and climb the nearest beacon ladder; first crossing on foot is recommended.
quote: offices of tourism in Beauvoir-sur-Mer and Noirmoutier provide precise tide schedules, more reliable than random search results... if the tide rises faster than expected... Immediately abandon the vehicle if necessary and reach the nearest safety beacon by climbing the ladder... for initial contact, crossing on foot remains most instructive.

claim: The Foulées du Gois footrace, founded by Jo Cesbron in 1986 and held every June since 1987, has runners race against the incoming tide; the 2026 edition is on Monday 15 June.
quote: The idea for a race on the Passage du Gois was conceived in the late stages of 1986, with Jo Cesbron as the founding president of the 'Foulées du Gois'. Since June 1987 once a year 'les Foulées du Gois' takes place.

claim: Six of the nine balises are 'mâts de perroquet' (parrot masts) with iron rungs sealed in a masonry cone; the other three are ladder beams topped by a hexagonal railed platform called a hune.
quote: Six balises are called 'mats de perroquet' - they are beams pierced by different iron rungs and sealed in a masonry cone. The three other balises consist of two beams connected by rungs to form a ladder... with a hexagonal platform with railings at the top called the cage or hune.

claim: Safe-crossing rule of thumb: with a tidal coefficient above 70, cross 1h30 either side of low tide; with a medium coefficient (50–70), restrict crossing to 30 min to 1 hour either side.
quote: If the tidal coefficient is high (more than 70), it's recommended to cross the Passage du Gois 1h30 minutes before and after the low tide of the day. If the tidal coefficient is medium (between 50 and 70), crossing is recommended 30 minutes to 1 hour before and after the low tide.

claim: Noirmoutier has 83 km of cycling paths and three signed thematic loops: From Beaches to Harbours (19.2 km), From Marshes to Mills (18.5 km) and From Gois to Forests (23.3 km), with 11 rental points and 3,000 bikes available.
quote: From Beaches to Harbours - 19.2 km (~2 hours)... From Marshes to Mills - 18.5 km... From Gois to Forests - 23.3 km... Total cycling paths: 83 km... 11 rental points with 3,000 bikes available

claim: Noirmoutier connects to the Vélodyssée (EuroVelo 1) via the Fromentine bridge cycle lane or the Passage du Gois at low tide, with the Bois de la Chaise loop linking the castle, the elegant villas, Plage des Dames and the L'Herbaudière fishing port.
quote: The island is accessible via La Vélodyssée route through two options... Fromentine bridge with cycle lane (safer alternative)... Bois de la Chaise district featuring elegant villas and the renowned Plage des Dames, plus the fishing port of L'Herbaudière

claim: Standard adult bike rental on Noirmoutier runs €8–18/day (€40–90/week) and e-bikes €20–40/day (€95–210/week), with shops in Barbâtre (NO 2 Roo), La Guérinière (No'vélo), L'Épine (Les Vélos de Paul) and Noirmoutier-en-l'Île (Vel'hop, L'Île à Vélo); L'Herbaudière is served by seasonal delivery only.
quote: Standard bikes (VTC): €8–12 (low season) to €14–18 (high season). E-bikes (VAE): €20–28 (low season) to €30–40 (high season)... L'Herbaudière: No service on-site; Vel'hop & No'vélo deliver seasonally

claim: Maximum Glisse, based at Port du Morin in L'Épine, runs a full multi-discipline school covering kitesurf, wingfoil, windsurf, catamaran, kayak, SUP and e-foil, and organises Raid catamaran trips around Noirmoutier on 6–7 and 20–21 June 2026.
quote: Main Base: Port du Morin, Digue SUD, L'Epine, Île de Noirmoutier... Sailing, Kitesurf, Wingfoil, Windsurfing, SUP, Kayak, Catamaran, E-foil... Raid 1 scheduled for June 6-7, 2026... Raid 2 scheduled for June 20-21, 2026

claim: Mouv'n Kite, the kitesurf school at the foot of the Noirmoutier bridge in Barbâtre, is open daily 7:45 AM–10 PM from March to November, making Barbâtre the island's main beginner kite spot.
quote: Mouv'n Kite welcomes students from March to November, 7 days a week, between 7:45 AM and 10 PM, depending on wind conditions. Barbâtre is considered the ideal beginner spot

claim: Sand-yachting (char à voile) on Noirmoutier is run by Sel ton Char from Plage de l'Océan in Barbâtre (and Plage de la Croix Rouge in July–August), open daily March to November for ages 8 and up under a state-certified instructor.
quote: Plage de l'océan (September 1 - June 31)... Plage de la Croix Rouge (July 1 - August 31)... de mars à novembre tous les jours... Activities begin at age 8 and up

claim: The Centre Nautique Municipal Fort Saint-Pierre at Plage des Dames is the island's largest sailing school, offering age-graded stages from 4 to 15+, a Topcat Avanti sport catamaran and foiling-dinghy (Birdyfish) instruction, with summer-program registration opening mid-March 2026.
quote: Avenue Georges Clemenceau - Plage des Dames, 85330 Noirmoutier-en-l'Île... Topcat Avanti, described as a 13.5-foot sport catamaran ideal for learning and advancement... Pas de stages de printemps - Prochains stages cet été... summer program registration opening mid-March 2026

claim: Hissez-Haut, the French Sailing Federation school in Barbâtre, takes children from age 5 on Optimist, Topaz and Hobie Cat 16 catamarans, windsurfing and wingfoil.
quote: Hissez-haut, a sailing school affiliated with the French Sailing Federation located in Barbâtre, welcomes children from age 5 and offers different supports including Optimist, Topaz and Hobie Cat 16 Catamarans, windsurfing and Wingfoil

claim: Noirmoutier Evasion rents double sea-kayaks at €25/1 h or €45/2 h per person and runs a guided 2-hour Escape Kayak with waterproof road-book bag for €30 per person, with wetsuit hire at €5.
quote: Escape Kayak (Guided Activity)... Duration: 2 hours, Cost: €30 per person... Double Kayak Rental: 1 hour: €25 per person, 2 hours: €45 per person... Wetsuits... €5 per person

claim: The Centre Équestre Horse Club de L'Herbaudière, 145 route de l'Herbaudière, is open 1 April–11 November 2026 and runs 2-hour morning beach rides governed by tide schedules (reserved for advanced riders) plus rides through the Luzéronde forest and salt marshes.
quote: 145 route de l'Herbaudière, 85330 Noirmoutier-en-l'île... Du 1 April 2026 au 11 November 2026... Two-hour beach rides are organized in the mornings based on tide schedules but are reserved for advanced riders

claim: At Marais salant Les Coûts, saunier Philippe offers free guided visits mornings 11:00–12:30 and afternoons by reservation, mid-June to end of September, with direct sale of gross salt and fleur de sel.
quote: Philippe, saunier depuis 28 ans, propose des visites gratuites et explicatives du fonctionnement du marais salant le matin de 11h à 12h30 et l'après-midi sur réservation. Ouvert du 15 juin au 30 septembre 2026.

claim: Marais salant La Nouvelle Brille runs free saunier-led tours daily without reservation from March to September at 5pm (twice daily in July–August), with direct sale of fleur de sel, gros sel, salicorne and salt-mustard.
quote: Visites guidées gratuites sans réservation de mars à septembre à 17h chaque jour, et de juillet à août à 11h30 et 17h chaque jour. Vente directe de gros sel, sel moulu, fleur de sel, salicorne.

claim: L'Esprit Saunier, the direct-sale shop of the Coopérative de sel de Noirmoutier, is at 1 rue Piet in Noirmoutier-en-l'Île and stocks the cooperative's full hand-harvested salt range.
quote: The shop of the Noirmoutier Salt Cooperative is located at 1 rue Piet in Noirmoutier-en-Île, in the heart of the island and close to the town center. Discover the world of salt producers and an authentic selection of sea salts.

claim: Founded in 1942, the Coopérative de sel de Noirmoutier groups ~100 producer-sauniers operating more than 2,300 salt ponds on the island.
quote: Founded in 1942, the Salt Cooperative of Noirmoutier brings together about a hundred associated producers who operate more than 2,300 salt ponds on the island of Noirmoutier.

claim: Nine oyster bars dot the island, including La Jane at the port de plaisance de L'Herbaudière (oysters paired with wine) and Le Bouclard des Petits Bassets, Chez P'tit Louis and La Godaille around La Guérinière's Port du Bonhomme.
quote: La Jane – Port de plaisance de l'Herbaudière. Oysters paired with wine, overlooks the pleasure marina. Le Bouclard des Petits Bassets – 5 chemin des Places. Chez P'tit Louis – Port du Bonhomme.

claim: Le Bouclard in La Guérinière offers ostréiculteur-led farm visits Monday–Saturday (closed Tuesday) at 10:30am from April to October, ending in a tasting of six oysters; 2025 rate was 12 € per person.
quote: Visite sur demande selon disponibilité, en semaine (sauf le mardi) à 10h30, environ 1h de visite suivie de la dégustation, tarif 2025 : 12 € par personne. Tasting of 6 oysters or fish rillettes.

claim: Bouin's oysters joined the Sites Remarquables du Goût label in 2023; the commune's four ports — des Brochets, des Champs, de la Louippe and du Bec (Port chinois) — host roughly 180 active oyster farms.
quote: Depuis 2023, la commune de Bouin fait partie des Sites Remarquables du Goût pour ses huîtres. Quatre ports sont propices à l'ostréiculture : port des Brochets, Port des Champs, port de la Louippe et port du Bec.

claim: Bouin sits inside the Baie de Bourgneuf with about 200 oyster farmers; several open their cabanes for visits and tastings, and the first Sunday of August hosts the Fête des gobeurs d'huîtres.
quote: Parmi les 200 ostréiculteurs qui élèvent les huîtres en baie de Bourgneuf, certains organisent des visites et dégustations « à la cabane ». Le premier dimanche d'août, fête des gobeurs d'huîtres.

claim: The Bonnotte was brought to Noirmoutier from Barfleur (Manche) in the 1920s–30s, abandoned around 1960 because hand-harvesting was unprofitable, then revived in 1995 by the Coopérative Agricole de Noirmoutier with INRA Brest.
quote: Sa production avait été abandonnée à l'arrivée de la mécanisation, car trop fragile et petite, la Bonnotte devait être ramassée à la main. La Coopérative Agricole de Noirmoutier s'est tournée vers l'INRA de Brest pour la recréer; les Noirmoutrins ont pu, dès 1995, replanter les semences.

claim: On 20 April 1996 a 5 kg lot of Bonnottes was sold at Hôtel Drouot in Paris for 15,000 francs (€500/kg), with proceeds donated to Les Restaurants du Cœur — the Guinness record for most expensive potato.
quote: On 20 April 1996, during an auction at the Hotel Drouot in Paris, a lot of 5 kg of bonnottes was bought by a private individual for 15,000 francs (€500 per kilogram). Proceeds were given to Les Restaurants du Cœur.

claim: Bonnotte and other early Noirmoutier potatoes can be bought at the island's farmers' markets or directly at the Coopérative Agricole de Noirmoutier, with the Bonnotte available only in limited quantities in early May.
quote: Early potatoes can be purchased at the island's farmers' markets or from the agricultural cooperative in Noirmoutier-en-l'Île. They are only available in limited quantities in early May every year.

claim: On the island the headline markets in 2026 are Noirmoutier-en-l'Île Place de la République (Fridays year-round, Tue/Sun 5 Apr–27 Sep) and Port de l'Herbaudière (6 Apr–21 Sep); La Guérinière trades Thursdays year-round and Sundays Apr–Oct.
quote: Place de la République: Fridays year-round; Tuesdays and Sundays (April 5 – September 27). Port de l'Herbaudière: April 6 – September 21, 2026. La Guérinière, Place des Lauriers: Thursdays year-round; Sundays (April-October).

claim: L'Étier, built on the site of a former oyster cabin on the Étier de l'Arceau, is listed in the Michelin Guide for its seafood-driven cuisine — langoustines, mayonnaise spider crab, marsh eels, sole meunière, Grand Marnier soufflé.
quote: L'Étier relies on the finest products from the coast, livestock and market gardens, offering langoustines cooked to perfection, mayonnaise spider crab, marsh eels with fine herb jus, sole meunière, Grand Marnier soufflé.

claim: L'Ételle, the gastronomic restaurant of Hôtel Fleur de Sel renamed in 2023, is run by chef Éric Pichou (30+ years' experience) and recognised by Michelin and Gault & Millau (2 toques), with a terrace facing the medieval castle and Saint-Philbert church.
quote: Le chef Éric Pichou élabore une cuisine raffinée qui honore les produits de la mer et le terroir de Noirmoutier. L'Ételle est classé au guide Michelin rouge et au Gault & Millau (2 toques).

claim: Le Grand Four, hidden behind a 17th-century building at 1 rue de la Cure in Noirmoutier-en-l'Île, has a Michelin star and a Gault & Millau listing, with a signature blue lobster menu around €75.
quote: Le Grand Four tient les promesses de son étoile Michelin. La spécialité du chef est son menu Homard Bleu, sublime, dont le tarif le réserve pour une occasion spéciale -75 euros-. Inscrit au prestigieux guide Gault et Millau.

claim: Hôtel Punta Lara's restaurant L'Atlantide in La Guérinière offers refined seafood cooking by chef André Goedde, leveraging the property's bayside terrace as a sunset alternative to L'Herbaudière.
quote: Restaurant L'Atlantide offers refined cuisine inspired by seafood and local ingredients, with Chef André Goedde and his team pursuing excellence.

claim: In 2026 Yeu Continent runs 6–8 daily crossings each way between Fromentine and Port-Joinville (Île d'Yeu) with a 30-minute crossing; Compagnie Vendéenne takes 45 minutes.
quote: Yeu Continent: '30' minutes; Compagnie Vendéenne: '45' minutes. 6–8 traversées/jour/direction

claim: Compagnie Yeu Continent advertises a 30% 'escapade' discount on same-day round trips, explicitly promoting day trips to Île d'Yeu from Fromentine.
quote: TARIFS ESCAPADES ! -30 % Sur un aller-retour dans la journée

claim: On a day trip to Île d'Yeu, a 14 km ride between the two main ports takes roughly 2h30, while the full island loop is around 6 hours by bike.
quote: A section between the two ports is about 14 km long and takes about 2 hours 30 minutes—ideal if you're only on the island for the day

claim: Bike rentals are clustered at Port-Joinville on arrival, with classic, mountain, electric bikes and tandems available from operators with long experience at around €15/day.
quote: You'll easily find the tourist office and lots of bike rental companies on the port upon your arrival

claim: Le Daviaud écomusée at La Barre-de-Monts opens 10 April to 6 September 2026, presenting the Marais Breton-Vendéen as France's largest open-air museum with bourrines, salt marshes, yoles and ningle-jumping demos.
quote: Ouvert du 10 avril au 6 septembre 2026 ... le plus grand musée de plein air de l'Ouest

claim: Le Daviaud is a Musée de France with a 250 m² 'Le Marais et les Hommes' gallery, audioguide in English, Accueil Vélo label and July–August catering with local produce.
quote: galerie de 250 m² 'Le Marais et les Hommes' ... label Accueil Vélo

claim: Bouin is the leading oyster production site on France's Atlantic coast with over 150 oyster operations, and joined the 'Sites Remarquables du Goût' list in 2023.
quote: Bouin est le premier site ostréicole de la côte atlantique avec plus de 150 entreprises ostréicoles

claim: Beauvoir-sur-Mer hosts the mainland end of the Gois and is the start point for the annual Foulées du Gois foot race timed against the incoming tide.
quote: Les Foulées du Gois ... une course à pied unique ... contre la marée montante

claim: L'Évasion 3 runs two daily round-trips between Pornic (Noëveillard) and L'Herbaudière (~1 hour each way), with 09:30/18:00 from Pornic and 10:45/19:15 from L'Herbaudière, making Pornic an easy boat day-trip from Noirmoutier.
quote: 2 allers-retours par jour ... départs de Pornic à 9h30 et 18h00 ... départs de L'Herbaudière à 10h45 et 19h15

claim: By road, Noirmoutier-en-l'Île to La Barre-de-Monts/Fromentine is about 19.6–20 km via the Pont de Noirmoutier, putting both inside the 30 km radius from L'Herbaudière.
quote: distance de 19,6 km ... environ 20 km

claim: The Marais Breton-Vendéen (locally 'le Marô') covers ~45,000 ha across 18 communes, is Natura 2000-classified, and is a major migratory stopover for spoonbills, egrets, herons, lapwings and stilts.
quote: le Marais Breton Vendéen ... 45 000 hectares ... classé Natura 2000

claim: The Marais Breton-Vendéen can be explored on foot, by bike, on horseback or on the water by canoe, paddle, kayak or traditional flat-bottomed yole.
quote: découvrir la biodiversité ... en canoë, paddle, kayak ... ou en yole

claim: Noirmoutier in June averages 17.2°C with highs near 18-20°C and lows 14-16°C; June is the driest month with about 42 mm of rain.
quote: Throughout June, Noirmoutier-en-l'Île averages a temperature of 17.2°C | 63°F. ... The driest month is June, with 42 mm | 1.7 inch of rainfall.

claim: June in Noirmoutier has the highest daily sunshine of any month, averaging about 10.16 hours, with humidity 47-59%.
quote: June features humidity ranging from 47% to 59%. The month that experiences a maximum number of daily hours with bright sunshine is June exhibiting an average duration of approximately 10.16 hours per day.

claim: Average June sea temperature at Noirmoutier is 17.3°C — swimmable but cool; the proper bathing season runs July-August.
quote: June average water temperature in Noirmoutier is 17.3°C.

claim: On 6-7 June 2026 sunrise is around 06:14-06:15 and sunset around 21:59-22:00, giving roughly 15h45 of daylight.
quote: June 6, 2026: Sunrise: 6:15 AM, Sunset: 9:59 PM... June 7, 2026: Sunrise: 6:14 AM, Sunset: 10:00 PM

claim: Tide coefficients at L'Herbaudière for the weekend of 6-7 June 2026 are weak (54/52 Sat, 50/48 Sun), dropping to 47 on Monday — i.e. neap tides, modest tidal range.
quote: June 6, 2026 (Norbert): Coefficient 54, 52 ... June 7, 2026 (Gilbert): Coefficient 50, 48 ... June 8, 2026 (Médard): Coefficient 47, 47

claim: Low-tide windows for the Passage du Gois on 6-7 June 2026 are roughly 03:37 and 15:49 (Sat) and 04:21 and 16:35 (Sun) — the afternoon slot is the practical crossing window.
quote: Saturday, June 6: Low tide: 03:37 (1.72 m) and 15:49 (1.87 m) ... Sunday, June 7: Low tide: 04:21 (1.78 m) and 16:35 (1.92 m)

claim: The Passage du Gois is drivable from about 1h30 before to 1h30 after low tide.
quote: the passage linking the mainland to the island of Noirmoutier is accessible by car 1h30 before to 1h30 after low tide

claim: Fête de la Bonnotte 2026 falls on Saturday 9 May — i.e. it is over before a 6-7 June visit; the bonnotte potato season itself still runs into June.
quote: 9 mai 2026 - Fête de la Bonnotte

claim: The Triathlon de Noirmoutier is scheduled for 6-7 June 2026 and will affect island roads and parts of the coast that weekend.
quote: Du 6 June 2026 au 7 June 2026 ... Triathlon de Noirmoutier

claim: World Ocean Day is marked on the island on Monday 8 June 2026 with a 09:30-12:00 programme at Plage des Dames.
quote: 8 juin 2026 - Journée mondiale de l'océan

claim: The Musée des Traditions de l'Île at La Guérinière (salt-marsh and maritime heritage) is on shoulder-season hours until 26 June 2026 — afternoons only, 14:00-17:30, Tuesday to Saturday, so closed Sunday and Monday in early June.
quote: From April 7 to June 26, it is open in the afternoon from 14:00 to 17:30 Tuesday to Saturday
